foreignObject.div: Figure 11. The tier's payoff is generation, and the third column is why. Five arms at 24,000 steps; the first two columns are 5 draws of 128 apiece, the third is the D4 orbit oracle pointed at 48 samples per checkpoint instead of at a corpus. The flat transformed arms miss the corpus's length distribution by 25–112% of a program's own length and keep an orbit in 13–23% of draws where the corpus has one in 100%; the same scenes spelled with REPEATX keep one in 48 of 48. So the over-long samples are not the model continuing the orbit — it is losing the orbit and filling the space with new content. Teacher-forced a mirrored copy costs 3% of its own original; free-running the same checkpoint draws one in 13% of samples. The control's translated copies survive in 40–67%, so transformed reuse is harder to generate than translated reuse while being equally easy to predict. EMD is normalised by each corpus's own mean length — the weaker, relative column.
